notes: Windows: a crew pointer is on screen only while its agent works. The resting pointer that showed only a name is gone: nobody working means nobody on screen.
A pointer on screen always moves. It sways around its spot in a slow figure of eight and hops at every new step.
It says "done" when the agent finishes and leaves 2 seconds later. An agent Buddy hears nothing from for 30 seconds leaves.
During a long command the pointer stays with its text, for as long as Buddy can see the step has not ended, up to 10 minutes.
When an agent needs you: an agent that asks you a question, or a tool that posts "state": "waiting", stays on screen, says so and hops every 1.5 seconds until you answer.
Fixed: an OpenCode pointer keeps its own name when it says done.
Cost: the motion uses some CPU while agents work, about 1 % to 5 % of one core for each pointer on the test PC.

Not checked: Claude Code and Codex with a live session (recorded samples only), and a real question from an agent. An agent that waits for you to allow a command shows that command's line, not "Needs you": the agents do not record that they wait for a click.
